## About the Course

**KJK StatScript** is an educational platform designed to bridge theoretical probability, computational data science, and East African macroeconomic policy.

- **Module Focus:** Moving from abstract textbook examples (dice, cards, urns) to empirical, measure-theoretic probability grounded in real-world data.
- **Pedagogical Approach:** **"Just-In-Time" Syntax Callouts.** Programming concepts are introduced at the exact moment they are required to solve a statistical problem, ensuring complete beginners can follow along in RStudio without losing sight of the underlying mathematics.
- **Core Objective of Episode 1.5:** To translate Kolmogorov's Axioms of Probability—established theoretically in Episode 1.2—into executable R code (`tidyverse`, `ggplot2`) within a Quarto publication environment using a 45.8-year East African climate time series.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## About the Dataset

### Overview

This document analyzes the **Kampala Subnational Dekadal Rainfall Dataset (1981–2026)**, derived from the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) Vulnerability Analysis and Mapping (VAM) data engine and the Climate Hazards Group InfraRed Precipitation with Stations (**CHIRPS**).

### Technical & Geographic Specifications

- **Geographic Unit:** Kampala District, Uganda
- **Administrative Hierarchy:** Administrative Level 2 (`adm_level = 2`)
- **UN OCHA Place Code (PCODE):** `UG1002` (`adm_id = 999571`)
- **Spatial Grid Resolution:** `n_pixels = 19` ($\approx$ 475 $km^2$ spatial aggregation across 5 km * 5 km satellite cells)
- **Temporal Resolution:** **Dekads (10-Day Intervals)**
  - Dekad 1: Days 1–10 of the month (`YYYY-MM-01`)
  - Dekad 2: Days 11–20 of the month (`YYYY-MM-11`)
  - Dekad 3: Day 21 to the end of the month (`YYYY-MM-21`)
- **Sample Space Dimension (**N): **1,650 dekads** (36 dekads/year across 45.8 years from January 1981 to October 2026)

### Data Dictionary

| Variable Name | Data Type | Units / Format | Description |
|:-----------------|:-----------------|:-----------------|:-----------------|
| `date` | `character` / `Date` | `MM/DD/YYYY` | Start date of the 10-day dekad |
| `adm_level` | `integer` | Category (`2`) | Administrative boundary tier (Level 2 = District) |
| `adm_id` | `integer` | Numeric ID | Unique WFP database identifier (`999571`) |
| `PCODE` | `character` | String Code | UN OCHA standardized spatial code (`UG1002`) |
| `n_pixels` | `integer` | Integer Count | Number of satellite grid cells covering the district (`19`) |
| `rfh` | `double` | Millimeters ($mm$) | **Rainfall Height:** Observed dekadal precipitation |
| `rfh_avg` | `double` | Millimeters ($mm$) | **Historical Baseline:** 30-year dekadal mean |
| `rfq` | `double` | Percentage ($\%$) | **Rainfall Anomaly Ratio:** $\left(\frac{\text{rfh}}{\text{rfh\_avg}}\right) \times 100\%$ |

## Environment Setup & Data Loading

::: {.callout-note title="R Micro-Hint 1: Packages & Tidy Data Frames"}
- **`library(tidyverse)`**: Loads the Tidyverse ecosystem, including `dplyr` (data manipulation), `readr` (fast data loading), and `ggplot2` (graphics).
- **`read_csv()`**: Imports CSV files into a **tibble** (an enhanced R data frame that prints cleanly without flooding your console).
- **`nrow()`**: Measures the total number of rows (N) in an R data object.
:::

```{r}
#| label: setup-data
#| message: false
#| warning: false

library(tidyverse)

# Load Kampala Dekadal Dataset (1981 - 2026)
df <- read_csv("Kampala_Dekad_Data_since_1981_to_2026.csv")

# Measure Total Sample Space Size (N = 1,650 dekads)
N <- nrow(df)

cat("Total Sample Space Size (N):", N, "dekads\n\n")

# Preview data structure
head(df %>% select(date, PCODE, n_pixels, rfh, rfh_avg, rfq), 5)
```

## Variable Selection & Event Masking

From Episode 1.2, we define our sample space ($\Omega$ or S) as all observed Kampala dekads ($N = 1,650$). We set up the following disjoint and non-disjoint events based on rainfall height extracted into a dedicated vector (`rfh_mm <- df$rfh`):

- **Event** $A$ (Wet Dekad): $\text{rfh\_mm} \ge 20.0\text{ mm}$
- **Event** $A^c$ (Dry / Low-Rain Dekad): $\text{rfh\_mm} < 20.0\text{ mm}$
- **Event** $B$ (Heavy Rain Dekad): $\text{rfh\_mm} \ge 50.0\text{ mm}$
- **Event** $C$ (Moderate Rain Dekad): $20.0\text{ mm} \le \text{rfh\_mm} < 50.0\text{ mm}$

::: {.callout-note title="R Micro-Hint 2: Vector Extraction & Tidy Mutation"}
- **`rfh_mm <- df$rfh`**: The `$` operator extracts a single column as an atomic vector.
- **`mutate()`**: Adds new variables or modifies existing ones while preserving existing columns.
- **Logical Operators (`>=`, `<`, `&`)**: Evaluate conditions element-by-element, returning logical vectors of `TRUE` and `FALSE`.
:::

```{r}
#| label: event-masking

# Select target precipitation variable
rfh_mm <- df$rfh

# Define boolean event vectors inside data frame
df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    is_wet      = rfh_mm >= 20.0,                        # Event A
    is_dry      = rfh_mm < 20.0,                         # Event A^c
    is_heavy    = rfh_mm >= 50.0,                        # Event B
    is_moderate = (rfh_mm >= 20.0) & (rfh_mm < 50.0)     # Event C
  )

# Display sample event mask table
head(df %>% select(rfh, is_wet, is_dry, is_heavy, is_moderate), 10)

```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Computing Empirical Probabilities
::: {.callout-note title="R Micro-Hint 3: Logical Averaging with mean() and summarise()"}
In R, `TRUE` coerces to `1` and `FALSE` coerces to `0`. Passing a logical vector to `mean()` calculates $\frac{\sum \text{TRUE}}{N}$, yielding the empirical probability $P(E)$. `summarise()` collapses thousands of rows into a single summary table.
:::


```{r}
#| label: compute-probabilities

# Summarize proportions and absolute event counts
prob_summary <- df %>%
  summarise(
    p_A  = mean(is_wet),
    p_Ac = mean(is_dry),
    p_B  = mean(is_heavy),
    p_C  = mean(is_moderate),
    n_A  = sum(is_wet),
    n_Ac = sum(is_dry),
    n_B  = sum(is_heavy),
    n_C  = sum(is_moderate)
  )

# Extract scalar probabilities
p_A  <- prob_summary$p_A
p_Ac <- prob_summary$p_Ac
p_B  <- prob_summary$p_B
p_C  <- prob_summary$p_C

cat("Empirical Dekadal Probabilities (N = 1,650)\n")
cat(sprintf("P(A)   [Wet Dekad (>=20mm)]:       %.4f  (%.2f%%) | Count: %d\n", p_A, p_A * 100, prob_summary$n_A))
cat(sprintf("P(A^c) [Dry Dekad (<20mm)]:        %.4f  (%.2f%%) | Count: %d\n", p_Ac, p_Ac * 100, prob_summary$n_Ac))
cat(sprintf("P(B)   [Heavy Rain (>=50mm)]:      %.4f  (%.2f%%) | Count: %d\n", p_B, p_B * 100, prob_summary$n_B))
cat(sprintf("P(C)   [Moderate Rain (20-50mm)]:  %.4f  (%.2f%%) | Count: %d\n", p_C, p_C * 100, prob_summary$n_C))

```

## Programmatic Verification of Kolmogorov's Axioms

We test whether our empirical estimates satisfy Kolmogorov's foundational rules derived in Episode 1.2:

1.  **Axiom 1 & 2 (Non-negativity & Normalization):** $0 \le P(E) \le 1$ and $P(\Omega) = 1.0$.
2.  **Proof 1 — The Complement Rule:** $P(A) + P(A^c) = 1.0$.
3.  **Proof 2 — Additivity for Disjoint Sets:** Since $B \cap C = \emptyset$ and $A = B \cup C$:

$$P(A) = P(B \cup C) = P(B) + P(C)$$

4.  **Proof 3 — Monotonicity:** Since $B \subseteq A$ (Heavy rain is a subset of Wet dekads):

$$P(B) \le P(A)$$

::: {.callout-note title="R Micro-Hint 4: Safe Equality Testing with all.equal() and stopifnot()"}
Floating-point arithmetic can introduce microscopic rounding differences. In R, `all.equal(x, y)` checks if numbers are equal within machine precision tolerances, while `stopifnot()` halts script execution if a condition is `FALSE` (R's native equivalent of Python's `assert`).
:::


```{r}
#| label: verify-axioms

cat("Kolmogorov Axiom Verifications \n\n")

# Verification 1: Complement Rule P(A) + P(A^c) == 1.0
complement_sum <- p_A + p_Ac
cat("1. Complement Rule Check:\n")
cat(sprintf("   P(A) + P(A^c) = %.4f + %.4f = %.4f\n", p_A, p_Ac, complement_sum))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(complement_sum, 1.0)))
cat("   RESULT: Verified Mathematically (P(A^c) = 1 - P(A))\n\n")

# Verification 2: Additivity for Disjoint Sets P(B U C) == P(B) + P(C) == P(A)
disjoint_sum <- p_B + p_C
cat("2. Disjoint Additivity Check (A = B U C):\n")
cat(sprintf("   P(B) + P(C) = %.4f + %.4f = %.4f | P(A) = %.4f\n", p_B, p_C, disjoint_sum, p_A))
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(disjoint_sum, p_A)))
cat("   RESULT: Verified Mathematically (P(B U C) = P(B) + P(C))\n\n")

# Verification 3: Monotonicity Property (B subset of A => P(B) <= P(A))
cat("3. Monotonicity Check (B subset of A):\n")
cat(sprintf("   P(B) [%.4f] <= P(A) [%.4f] is %s (%.4f <= %.4f)\n", p_B, p_A, p_B <= p_A, p_B, p_A))
stopifnot(p_B <= p_A)
cat("   RESULT: Verified Mathematically (P(B) <= P(A))\n\n")

cat("STATUS: All Kolmogorov Probability Axioms Verified in R!\n")

```

## Sample Space Partition Visualization (`ggplot2`)

We construct a publication-ready graphic of the sample space partition $\Omega = 1,650\text{ dekads}$. The three disjoint event sets $A^c$ (Dry), $C$ (Moderate), and $B$ (Heavy) completely cover $\Omega$ without overlap:

$$\Omega = A^c \cup C \cup B \quad \implies \quad P(\Omega) = P(A^c) + P(C) + P(B) = 1.0$$

::: {.callout-note title="R Micro-Hint 5: Grammar of Graphics with ggplot2"}
- **`ggplot(data, aes(x, y, fill))`**: Initializes a plot canvas with mapping aesthetics.
- **`geom_col()`**: Creates bar plots representing pre-computed summary values.
- **`theme_minimal()`**: Applies a clean academic theme.
- **`ggsave()`**: Exports publication-quality raster or vector images (`dpi = 300`).
:::


```{r}
#| label: visualize-partition
#| fig-cap: "Partition of Sample Space Ω (Kampala Rainfall 1981–2026, N = 1,650 Dekads)"

# Prepare summary data frame for plotting
df_plot <- tibble(
  category = factor(
    c("Dry Dekad (A^c)", "Moderate Rain (C)", "Heavy Rain (B)"),
    levels = c("Dry Dekad (A^c)", "Moderate Rain (C)", "Heavy Rain (B)")
  ),
  probability = c(p_Ac * 100, p_C * 100, p_B * 100)
)

# Render ggplot chart
p <- ggplot(df_plot, aes(x = category, y = probability, fill = category)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.45, show.legend = FALSE) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sprintf("%.2f%%", probability)),
    vjust = -0.5,
    fontface = "bold",
    size = 3.8
  ) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("#e74c3c", "#3498db", "#2ecc71")) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 60), expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.05))) +
  labs(
    title = "Partition of Sample Space Ω (Kampala Rainfall 1981–2026, N = 1,650 Dekads)",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Probability (%)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(size = 11, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    axis.title.y = element_text(size = 10),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  )

# Export graphic for Episode 1.7 Academic Report Writing
ggsave("r_sample_space_partition.png", plot = p, width = 8, height = 5.5, dpi = 300)
print(p)

```

## Empirical Insights

An analysis of the **Kampala Subnational Dekadal Rainfall Dataset (1981–2026)** across $N = 1,650$ dekads yields the following key statistical properties:

- **High Baseline Probability of Rainfall (**$P(A) = 63.09\%$): Over the 45.8-year period, nearly two-thirds of all 10-day dekads in Kampala recorded at least $20.0\text{ mm}$ of rainfall ($n_A = 1,041\text{ dekads}$).
- **Moderate Rain Dominates the Sample Space (**$P(C) = 45.58\%$): Moderate dekadal rainfall ($20.0\text{ mm} \le \text{rfh} < 50.0\text{ mm}$) accounts for the largest partition of the sample space ($n_C = 752\text{ dekads}$), representing standard operational moisture levels.
- **Low Frequency of Heavy Rain / Flood Risk (**$P(B) = 17.52\%$): Dekads with extreme precipitation ($\text{rfh} \ge 50.0\text{ mm}$) occur in less than 1 in 5 dekads ($n_B = 289\text{ dekads}$), confirming that extreme events occupy a strict subset of total wet dekads.
- **Dry Dekad Occurrence (**$P(A^c) = 36.91\%$): Dry dekads ($\text{rfh} < 20.0\text{ mm}$) occur in approximately 37% of all observed periods ($n_{A^c} = 609\text{ dekads}$), reflecting Kampala's distinct bimodal dry season windows (January–February and June–July).

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Mathematical & Methodological Summary

This Quarto document successfully bridges measure-theoretic probability theory with practical R data engineering:

1.  **Axiomatic Soundness:** Kolmogorov's three probability axioms hold programmatically across the entire 45.8-year climate record:

- **Normalization:** $P(\Omega) = P(A^c \cup C \cup B) = 36.91\% + 45.58\% + 17.52\% = 100.0\%$.
- **Complement Rule:** $P(A) + P(A^c) = 0.6309 + 0.3691 = 1.0000$.
- **Additivity for Disjoint Sets:** $P(B \cup C) = P(B) + P(C) = 0.1752 + 0.4558 = 0.6309 = P(A)$.
- **Monotonicity:** $P(B) \le P(A) \implies 0.1752 \le 0.6309$.

2.  **Efficiency of Tidy Vectorization:** Using `dplyr::mutate()` combined with `mean()` provides an execution pattern that avoids slow R `for` loops when computing empirical probabilities across large vectors.
3.  **Reproducible Proofing:** Leveraging R's `stopifnot()` and `all.equal()` functions enforces mathematical verification in automated analytical pipelines, preventing bad data or silent errors from passing downstream into policy models.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Institutional & Practical Recommendations

### For Statistical Researchers & Students

- **Adopt Explicit Vector Extraction:** Always isolate target metric columns into dedicated vectors (e.g., `rfh_mm <- df$rfh`) before applying logical comparison masks to maintain clean, readable script architecture.
- **Export Visual Assets for Institutional Reports:** Save high-resolution chart exports (`ggsave("r_sample_space_partition.png", dpi = 300)`) directly into structured assets folders for cross-referencing in Microsoft Word and LaTeX document compilation (**Episode 1.7**).

### For Institutional Policy Analysts (UBOS, NPA, Bank of Uganda)

- **Integrate Dekadal Baselines into Climate Risk Planning:** Utilize the baseline probability $P(\text{rfh} \ge 20\text{mm}) = 63.09\%$ and heavy rainfall risk $P(\text{rfh} \ge 50\text{mm}) = 17.52\%$ to anchor agricultural monitoring, urban drainage planning under Uganda's **NDP IV**, and disaster resilience frameworks.
- **Maintain Automated Audit Trails:** Embed programmatic `stopifnot()` checks within automated data pipeline R scripts to verify statistical properties automatically whenever fresh dekadal data feeds are appended from CHIRPS or WFP sources.
